record.title: China Telecom team releases Xing4.0 MoE model trained on Ascend with MindSpore
record.summary: China Telecom’s XingChen-AGI team released Xing4.0-29B-A4B on September 17, 2026. Its official repository describes a 29B-total, 4B-active mixture-of-experts model trained on Ascend 910C using MindSpore, with 256K native context. The developers report roughly 96% higher training throughput after several optimizations, measured against their own out-of-box Ascend baseline. The repository also lists benchmark results, but this activation found no independent reproduction; neither claim establishes parity with CUDA systems or broad agent capability.
organizations: China Telecom Artificial Intelligence Technology Co., Ltd.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: The XingChen-AGI project published the Xing4.0-29B-A4B release entry dated 2026-09-17 and public model documentation.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The project describes a 29B-total/4B-active model, 256K native context, and training on Ascend 910C with MindSpore/MindFormers.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The developers report approximately 96% greater training throughput after co-optimization compared with their own out-of-box Ascend performance; this is not a comparison with CUDA/NVIDIA.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The repository reports model benchmark scores including 75.0 on SWE-bench Verified and 57.5 on Terminal-Bench 2.1; this activation did not reproduce the scores or audit their full protocols.

evidence_gaps.description: No independent group reproduced model benchmark results or training-throughput claims.
Original pretraining scale and economics are not established by the inspected README.
The model-weight license scope and upstream maturity of deployment integrations were not independently resolved.

brief.importance_rationale: If the reported end-to-end training and released model are technically sound, this is meaningful evidence that a modern sparse model can be trained and released using an alternative accelerator and software stack. A 6 reflects ecosystem and compute-diversification consequences; first-party benchmarks and throughput claims remain unreplicated, and pretraining scale and economics are not disclosed here.
limitations: The repository is first-party evidence for what the developers released and claim, not independent verification of training or performance.
The approximately 96% throughput uplift is measured against the authors’ own out-of-box Ascend baseline; it does not show superiority to NVIDIA/CUDA.
This source check did not establish original pretraining token count, cluster size, wall-clock, energy, achieved utilization, total cost or failures/restarts.
The README reports benchmark scores, but this activation did not inspect complete protocols or reproduce them.
Weight-license scope was not verified separately from the repository license; several inference framework changes are described as pending upstream PRs.
organizations: China Telecom Artificial Intelligence Technology Co., Ltd.
brief.summary: China Telecom’s XingChen-AGI team released Xing4.0-29B-A4B on September 17, 2026. Its official repository describes a 29B-total, 4B-active mixture-of-experts model trained on Ascend 910C using MindSpore, with 256K native context. The developers report roughly 96% higher training throughput after several optimizations, measured against their own out-of-box Ascend baseline. The repository also lists benchmark results, but this activation found no independent reproduction; neither claim establishes parity with CUDA systems or broad agent capability.

technical.claimed_result: Developers report about 96% throughput improvement over their out-of-box Ascend setup and publish agent/coding benchmark scores, including SWE-bench Verified 75.0 and Terminal-Bench 2.1 57.5.
technical.demonstrated_result: The official repository and dated release entry are public and document the model configuration, claimed results and deployment status. Performance was not independently tested in this activation.
technical.mechanism: The repository describes a sparse mixture-of-experts model using mHC, MLA and MTP, adapted to Ascend 910C with MindSpore/MindFormers. It attributes training-throughput gains to MoE communication tuning, selective recomputation, graph/operator fusion and fused mHC operators.
technical.regime: First-party documentation for the Xing4.0-29B-A4B release, Ascend 910C/MindSpore training and author-selected model benchmarks; not an independent or matched cross-hardware evaluation.
technical.strongest_baseline: For the throughput claim, the README names the developers’ out-of-box Ascend performance as baseline. No matched CUDA baseline was presented in the inspected material.

brief.title: China Telecom team releases Xing4.0 MoE model trained on Ascend with MindSpore
brief.why_it_matters: A public model release accompanied by a concrete end-to-end alternative-accelerator training account adds evidence about the maturity of non-CUDA AI stacks. If independently reproduced, the configuration and optimization claims could inform compute diversification. The stated throughput baseline is internal to the authors’ Ascend setup, and cluster scale, total pretraining cost and independent model quality remain unestablished.
